All of the workshop's **core materials in one place.** Each **module** pairs **1:1:1:1** across four layers — a slide-deck **lecture**, a long-form **book chapter** (reading), a hands-on **laptop tutorial** (on `ifnb`), and the matching **Talapas HPC script** (the same `ifnb` analysis as a SLURM batch job). Click straight through to any of them. Material *beyond* the workshop — prerequisite appendices, external papers, the from-raw-FASTQs pipeline — lives under [Additional Resources](Additional_Resources.qmd).

::: callout-important
**Downloading a tutorial?** The browser saves each `.qmd` with a trailing `.txt` (e.g. `…qmd.txt`). After saving, **drop the trailing `.txt`** so the name ends in `.qmd`, then open it in RStudio. (The `.txt` suffix stops the browser from rendering the source as a webpage.)
:::

## What's in each layer

- **Lecture** — the slide deck (reveal.js); the in-class summary of the topic.
- **Reading (chapter)** — the long-form prose "textbook" treatment, with worked examples and cross-references to the prerequisite [appendices](Resources_Folder/Reference_Material.html).
- **Tutorial** — a hands-on `.qmd`: **view** the rendered HTML to read along, or **download** the source to open in RStudio and run chunk by chunk (with *Think about it* prompts and collapsible answers). The laptop tutorials run on the laptop-friendly **`ifnb`** dataset.
- **Talapas script** — the *same* tutorial workflow as a streamlined R script you submit to UO's **Talapas** HPC cluster as a SLURM job. Each script is numbered to match its module.

::: callout-tip
**Recommended order.** Watch the lecture and read the chapter *before* working the matching tutorial: the lecture is the summary, the chapter is the detail, the tutorial is the runnable code, and the Talapas script scales it on the cluster.
:::

## The Talapas HPC track

The fourth leg of each module: the same `ifnb` analysis as **streamlined R scripts** you submit to Talapas as SLURM jobs — no raw FASTQs and no new dataset (script 01 loads `ifnb` straight from Bioconductor). Start with [Talapas 01 — SLURM Basics](Exercise_Folder/Talapas/Tutorial_Talapas_01_SLURM_Basics.html), then the [Talapas 03 — Analysis Pipeline](Exercise_Folder/Talapas/Tutorial_Talapas_03_Analysis_Pipeline.html) overview, which links every script and lists the submission commands (each runs through the wrapper <a href="Exercise_Folder/Talapas/scripts/run_rscript.sbatch" download>run_rscript.sbatch</a>, e.g. `sbatch run_rscript.sbatch 01_qc_preprocessing.R`).

::: callout-note
**Want the full pipeline from raw FASTQs** (BCL → Cell Ranger → counts → analysis) on a real 10x dataset? That's optional, self-paced material in [Additional Resources → Full Talapas RNA-seq Run from raw FASTQs](Additional_Resources.qmd).
:::

## Datasets

The laptop tutorials and the Talapas track both run on **`ifnb`**; Module 11 (Spatial) uses **`stxBrain`**, and the other bonus modules (09 scATAC, 10 WGCNA) have their own datasets. Full download URLs, the expected directory layout, and a disk-space budget are on the **[Datasets](Datasets.qmd)** page. A quick data dictionary for the two main objects:

### `ifnb` — Kang *et al.* 2017 (Modules 01–08)

Human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), **\~14k cells**, 10x Chromium 3′ v1, loaded via `muscData::Kang18_8vs8()`. Eight lupus donors, each split into a control and an interferon-β–stimulated aliquot — so it has a **real condition** *and* **real biological replicates**, which is what makes integration, pseudobulk DE, and differential abundance meaningful.

| Variable (cell metadata) | What it is |
|---|---|
| `stim` | Condition — `CTRL` or `STIM` (interferon-β, 6 h). The two samples we integrate. |
| `ind` (→ `donor`) | Donor ID — one of **8** lupus patients; the biological replicate for DE / DA. |
| `seurat_annotations` | Author-curated cell type (CD14/CD16 Mono, CD4/CD8 T, B, NK, DC, pDC, Mk…). |
| `nCount_RNA` | Total UMIs (transcripts) detected in the cell. |
| `nFeature_RNA` | Number of genes detected in the cell. |
| `percent.mt` | Percent of reads from mitochondrial genes (added during QC; a stress/quality flag). |

### `stxBrain` — 10x Visium adult mouse brain (Module 11)

A **spatial** dataset: each observation is a **spot** (a ~55 µm patch of tissue containing several cells), not a single cell, and every spot keeps its **x/y position** on the slide. Two sagittal sections — **anterior** and **posterior** — installed via `SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")`.

| Variable / slot | What it is |
|---|---|
| `nCount_Spatial` | Total UMIs captured under the spot. |
| `nFeature_Spatial` | Number of genes detected under the spot. |
| `orig.ident` / section | Which tissue section the spot belongs to (anterior vs posterior). |
| `images` slot | The H&E image plus each spot's pixel/tissue coordinates, used for spatial plots. |
